messages:
leah: heads up — product wants a way to show 'effective token cost' on the route card that includes both cache savings and a share of prefetch infrastructure cost. can we prototype?
tom: good idea. we currently report raw token spend and a separate prefetch ledger but nothing combined. propose a field `amortized_prefetch_credit` emitted per-invocation so the dashboard can compute effective_cost = raw_cost - amortized_prefetch_credit + allocated_infra_share.
rajesh: allocation rules matter. I'm seeing three reasonable algorithms: (A) hit-based: credit only routes that actually consumed cache hits, (B) trigger-based: credit the route that triggered the prefetch and none others, (C) epoch-amortized: spread prefetch cost across all routes that used results in a time window.
nina: from a customer perspective, (A) and (C) are preferable because they don't hide the benefit from downstream consumers. (B) leads to odd surprise when other routes benefit but don't show savings.
leah: product wants a toggle: "Per-trigger (conservative)" vs "Per-consumer (apportioned)" vs "Epoch-amortized (smoothed)". default should be apportioned unless we detect abusive patterns.
tom: technical constraints: prefetch events and invocation events are produced by different services. prefetch has prefetch_id and cost estimate; invocations reference prefetch_id when they re-use the KV/prefix. we'll need to join these in the batch aggregator and emit a per-route amortized number.
rajesh: sampling note: we sample full payloads on ~2% of traffic. any join must carry `sample_rate` and `sample_weight`. analytics should do weighted_aggregation so estimates are unbiased. also we'll keep a separate strict-count aggregator for enterprise customers where sampling is disabled.
nina: UX: show the effective token cost with an info chip: "includes cache credits + infra share". clicking shows breakdown: raw token, cache credit (apportioned), infra allocation, sample CI. also show a little badge when sampling-based data is low-confidence.
leah: can someone sketch the analytics query? we can iterate after that.
tom: rough spark SQL to join and allocate apportioned credits:
```sql
WITH prefetch AS (
  SELECT prefetch_id, cost_estimate, event_ts FROM prefetch_events WHERE event_ts >= :start
), uses AS (
  SELECT prefetch_id, route, SUM(tokens) AS tokens_used, SUM(sample_weight) AS weight FROM invocation_uses WHERE event_ts >= :start GROUP BY prefetch_id, route
), totals AS (
  SELECT prefetch_id, SUM(tokens_used) AS total_tokens FROM uses GROUP BY prefetch_id
)
SELECT u.route,
       SUM((u.tokens_used / t.total_tokens) * p.cost_estimate * u.weight) / SUM(u.weight) AS allocated_prefetch_cost
FROM uses u JOIN totals t USING (prefetch_id) JOIN prefetch p USING (prefetch_id)
GROUP BY u.route;
```
rajesh: that looks fine. we must guard divide-by-zero when total_tokens is null (only prefetch recorded but no sampled consumers). fallback to epoch-amortized in that case.
nina: telemetry request: add metric `route.effective_token_cost` (per minute), `route.prefetch_utilization` (percent), and `route.prefetch_confidence` (0-1). add alert if utilization drops >30% in 10m window.
omitted: build-bot: nightly-aggregator: run_id=agg-171000-01 status=success :white_check_mark:
leah: rollout plan: 1) backend emits `amortized_prefetch_credit` + sample_weight in nightly job (hidden flag) 2) UI supports toggle and confidence badge behind dev feature flag 3) run 14-day compare between apportioned vs epoch on a sample of routes and surface anomalies (diff > 15%) to product 4) enable gradual rollout and gate enterprise customers by opt-in.
tom: proto change: add optional fields to InvocationTelemetry proto: `amortized_prefetch_credit` (double), `prefetch_id` (string), `sample_rate` (double) — all backward compatible. I'll make PR.
rajesh: for stats CI we can calculate approximate normal CI from weighted sums, and separately run a bootstrap nightly for top-100 routes where accuracy matters. avoids expensive bootstraps across all routes.
nina: frontend will show 95% CI as a thin whisker under the effective token cost. also add a small "i" tooltip explaining sampling and allocation rules.
leah: outstanding decisions: default allocation algorithm and low-data fallback. product please weigh in but engineering should pick apportioned with epoch fallback.
nina: will mock UX and post screenshots in this thread tomorrow.
nina: ping @eng-sre for alert rule review.
leah: thanks — assigning tasks: tom (proto + query), rajesh (sampling math + CI), nina (mock UI + tooltip copy), me (experiment plan). we'll reconvene next sync. :rocket:
